# Release 2.31 final gate review

recommendation: APPROVE
confidence: Medium-high for the release candidate; not certification of external source media, provider behavior, or completed publication.
blockers: []

## Original intent and desired outcome

originalIntent: Finish integrating the remaining generalizable material from the supplied workbook, preserve the previously accepted storyboard/camera direction, finish QA, and then commit and push the update.

desiredOutcome: A release-ready 2.31 package with reusable procedures in existing owners, a complete source-text disposition audit, readable default-four pagination with an eight-panel ceiling, preserved canonical content and extraction safety, and honest evidence boundaries. The parent performs the authorized two commits and push after this gate; this reviewer does not certify those future operations as completed.

userOutcomeReview: The inspected candidate meets that release-readiness outcome. The additions cover loop seams, real-time checkpoints, spatial audio, mask alignment/polarity, frame provenance, endpoint input compatibility, allowed state changes, native-audio transport, continuous-take decomposition, and soft camera control. The canonical contract and its consumers preserve shared/offscreen dialogue and consequential reactions without imposing a cut pair per line. Scene rhythm, emotional distance and spatial relationships remain contextual design choices. Actual playback and image quality are explicitly distinct from text planning and structural checks.

## Candidate and review boundary

- Reviewed tree: `/tmp/contents-production-skills-release-231-1793349016727`.
- Observed HEAD: `8e0e3b41da7962dc94f43335d99840783c6acd44`.
- Observed candidate: 30 tracked modified files and three untracked audit/release records, matching the supplied file list. No commit or push was performed.
- The implementation worktree was not edited. The installed support manifest was read only as installation evidence.
- No JS eval tool is exposed in this reviewer. The equivalent SDK status call was made through Bun in the review tree. It returned `ULW_LOOP_PLAN_MISSING`, so the authorized fallback report location is used.
- The report is this reviewer's only authored artifact. Bounded repository tests used their disposable synthetic fixtures; no provider/media-generation service, source spreadsheet write, dependency installation, or publication was invoked.

## Criterion assessment

The following IDs label the criteria supplied in the review brief; they are not new product requirements.

| Criterion | Assessment and evidence |
|---|---|
| G1: Complete source-text audit and generalizable integration | PASS. Independently parsed the audit and checked every disposition range: 55 tabs, 235 ranges, 3,105 assigned rows, no overlapping assignments, and each tab's assignment count equals its declared nonempty-row count. The audit distinguishes 55 headers from 3,050 data rows. Read the integration report, closure list, limitations, and sampled detailed dispositions; inspected the production owners for all 11 listed closures. External source-text research was not repeated. |
| G2: Default four, supported ceiling eight, explicit single-sheet capacity eight | PASS. `video-production-assets/scripts/render_storyboard_sheet.py:78-79,742-819,832-839` separates the default from the ceiling and explicitly passes the ceiling in `render_sheet`. Existing CLI artifacts reproduce 4+4+1 and 8+1 for the same nine canonical panels. `validate_storyboard.py:513-519` retains its supported ceiling rather than rejecting denser explicit layouts. |
| G3: Preserve IDs/order, source provenance, split extraction, and safe output behavior | PASS. Runtime changes are limited to density selection and documentation, not pixel processing or atomic output mechanics. Independently verified the two retained extraction manifests' nine-panel order and all 27 sheet/scene/panel SHA-256 values. Inspected the unchanged hard-link no-overwrite path and rollback at renderer lines 701-722 and 794-802. The independently passing affected suites exercise corruption, path escape, dangling links, existing output, malformed density, simulated post-preflight collision, scene bands, extraction, and final packaging. |
| G4: Preserve scene/shot/panel/sheet distinction and contextual craft | PASS. `storyboard-contract.md:48-111,123-134`, the storyboard skill, shot/edit templates, timing handoff, and QA consumers retain canonical content, held/shared/offscreen framing, intentional static/repeated treatment, and separate text/image/playback evidence. No new scene or panel quota is introduced. |
| G5: No schema, parallel production ledger, static vendor catalog, or new execution authority | PASS. Added tables are explicitly existing-document handoff slots; project schema and runtime registries are not changed. Provider-specific support remains conditional on actual endpoint verification. No dependency or executable integration with a new provider is introduced. |
| G6: Release metadata and historical evidence | PASS. `manifest.json:3` is 2.31; `CHANGELOG.md:5-11` is the dated promoted release section. Version checker reports package 2.31 with 26 consistent skills. The source audit deliberately retains package 2.30 historical validation. No unrelated skill-frontmatter bump was made. |
| G7: QA evidence is present and accurately scoped | PASS with the evidence limitations below. Both full-suite logs exist and record exit 0, 402 passed and 518 subtests. The actual CLI script, log, retained split manifests and all five captures exist. I opened all five captures: ordering and Korean captions are visible without observed clipping; the eight-panel preview is substantially denser. These are synthetic layout fixtures, not art, rhythm, linked-media, or provider-quality certification. |

6. Read the installed support manifest at `/home/declan/.codex/skills/video-production-assets/support/manifest.json`: version 2.31. The supplied installed-sync log records exit 0 and 78 preserved links; I did not rerun installation or independently recount all 78 links.

## Direct remove-ai-slops / programming review

Loaded `/home/declan/.omo/binary-runtime/5.1.35/plugin/skills/remove-ai-slops/SKILL.md`, `/home/declan/.omo/binary-runtime/5.1.35/plugin/skills/programming/SKILL.md`, and its Python reference. Applied their review criteria directly; their implementation/refactoring instructions do not override the read-only task or the explicit rule that pre-existing issues are notes.

- Excessive/useless tests: no finding in the addition. One test covers two adjacent canonical panel counts using real renderer output and input-derived expected order.
- Deletion-only/requested-removal tests: none added. No assertions merely pin the removal of the old dialogue policy.
- Tautological/implementation-mirroring tests: no new blocker. The default-density test checks observable sheet sizes and canonical IDs, not a constant or a source-code string. It would fail under the previous eight-panel default. PNG-bound metadata checks additionally observe the produced artifact.
- Prose-pinning: none added. The six JSON evaluation cases specify behavior under concrete prompts; they are not executable assertions requiring exact documentation wording, nor are they claimed as executed behavioral results.
- Test weakening: the explicit-eight updates retain the original single-sheet packaging fixture and explicit denser-layout assertions. The default behavior has separate coverage. No test was skipped, deleted, or disabled to pass.
- Determinism/mocks: the added test uses isolated temporary directories and no sleeps, polling, time assumptions, or mocks. The pre-existing collision test injects a deterministic late-output collision and asserts actual filesystem preservation/rollback; it is not evidence of a broad real-process concurrency stress test.
- Production extraction/parsing/normalization: none added. No new wrapper, parser, normalization path, dependency, fallback, or secondary ledger was introduced. The shared default constant is used at the paginated API and CLI seams; the explicit single-sheet entry point remains intentional.
- Maintenance/scope: existing untyped large renderer/validator modules and broad cleanup catches remain pre-existing characteristics, not a justification for an out-of-scope refactor. No newly introduced concrete safety or maintenance regression was found.
- Secrets/dependencies: no new credentials, secret-bearing config, dependency declarations, or network execution code was found in the supplied change and inspected candidate sections.

A separate code-review report and notepad path were not supplied and were not located in the review evidence. Therefore I cannot confirm another report explicitly includes the same skill-perspective/overfit checklist. This is an exact process-evidence gap, not a demonstrated failure of a stated product criterion; the direct review above is independently performed and does not claim that missing report exists.

## Nonblocking notes and exact evidence gaps

- The source audit records snapshot and review hashes, not a locally supplied complete raw workbook/segment-review archive. The gate verifies the audit's assignments, production integrations and honest boundaries, not an independent semantic reread of every external cell. No linked source media or live-provider verification is claimed.
- Full-suite 402/518 results and changed-link/anchor checks were inspected in the supplied logs/static record, not rerun in their entirety. The affected runtime suites, broad JSON parsing, audit coverage, retained image hashes and five visual captures were independently checked as described above.
- The six new storyboard evaluation prompts have no supplied response/transcript result set. They are evaluation definitions, not proof of measured agent improvement; the release documentation does not claim otherwise.
- `video-production-assets/assets/06-shots-template.md:36` retains a pre-existing example-level statement that camera direction stays DESIGN_PROPOSAL until support is checked. The updated canonical handoff at `references/11-ai-handoff.md:11` and its template distinguish adopted soft instructions from unchosen alternatives more precisely. This legacy wording is a note, not a newly caused regression under the supplied gate rule.
- Commit identities and remote push verification necessarily remain outside this pre-commit read-only gate. APPROVE means the reviewed candidate is suitable to proceed, not that the user's overall commit/push request is already complete.
